teams.heading: France winger Mickael Guillard calls Jiuta Wainiqolo 'a phenomenon' before Lyon
teams.body: France winger Mickael Guillard says France's focus is on the Flying Fijians in Lyon, not on world champions South Africa. Guillard spoke of Jiuta Wainiqolo, his club team-mate, as "a phenomenon" but said France know they cannot give him too much ball or space. Bayonne have also confirmed the release of tighthead prop Luke Tagi to join the Flying Fijians for the Nations Championship.

lead.why: It is the freshest Fiji-focused item in the pack, and it adds France's view of Jiuta Wainiqolo plus a new squad fact.

teams.heading: Seb Atkinson commits to Gloucester until 2029, turning down options to leave
teams.body: England centre Seb Atkinson has signed a new contract to stay at Gloucester until at least 2029, passing up options to leave the club, head coach George Skivington said. The 24-year-old has played seven times for England since his first cap in July 2025, and has started 79 of the 84 games he has played for Gloucester, who are currently top of the Premiership. Skivington said: "This is a really significant re-signing for us."

lead.why: A new England-related story about a current England centre's contract, rather than the squad-leaders item already run today or a pundit take.

teams.heading: Mickael Guillard says France have not discussed South Africa, focused on Fiji
teams.body: France winger Mickael Guillard says the squad has not discussed their clash with world champions South Africa, and that the focus is on the Nations Championship opener against Fiji in Lyon. “We’re focused on Fiji,” he told RugbyRama. He described the Flying Fijians as instinctive and very strong in open play, and said France must get back into position quickly whenever they lose possession. Guillard also said he is looking forward to facing his club team-mate Jiuta Wainiqolo.

lead.why: A France player's pre-match comments are a fresh story that the Fiji opener is the team's focus, and none of the day's other candidates is about the France squad.

teams.heading: James McNabney earns first Ireland call-up after ACL recovery with Ulster
teams.body: Ulster back row James McNabney, 23, was called into Andy Farrell's Ireland squad for the first time, learning of it while with Ulster in South Africa. He returned from an ACL injury in pre-season and said: "I was delighted. It was a big moment for the family as well." Having given up horse riding at 16 to play rugby, he could make his debut in November's Nations Championship fixtures.

lead.why: A first senior Ireland call-up for a back row returning from ACL injury is a fresh event, not a repeat of the Fiji A squad or the Furlong case.

teams.heading: Quesada expects Tommaso Allan at significant part of Friday training
teams.body: Tommaso Allan is building back from injury, and Gonzalo Quesada says he should take part in a significant part of Friday's training session, with a return to full work targeted for the following week. Allan is among the players being considered for the matchday squad, but Quesada says that decision depends on his condition. For Italy, his progress matters as the Azzurri open a run of four consecutive Tests against top-ten opposition, starting with South Africa.

lead.why: It adds a new storyline from Quesada's press conference, Tommaso Allan's rehabilitation, rather than repeating the already-reported count of 17 unavailable players.

teams.heading: Townsend says Scotland now believe they can beat All Blacks
teams.body: Scotland have never beaten New Zealand, and Gregor Townsend says that is no longer a mindset his squad carries. Speaking on the BBC Scotland Rugby Podcast, the coach contrasted his playing days, when he felt the Scots could never win, with his time in charge: 'I've not felt that as a coach.' Scotland face the All Blacks at Murrayfield in the Nations Championship, having lost all three of Townsend's previous meetings with them, the last 25-17 in 2025.

lead.why: Townsend's comments on Scotland's belief against New Zealand are the freshest team-centred story in the pack, and they come from the head coach himself.

teams.heading: Freddie Thomas says Wales omission gives him extra energy at Gloucester
teams.body: Gloucester lock Freddie Thomas has turned his omission from Steve Tandy's Wales squad into motivation. Thomas, who scored a try in Gloucester's win over Bath, said the call-up news was "really disappointing" but that it has given him "extra energy". He told BBC Radio Gloucestershire that Tandy was clear about the areas he must improve, and he believes his versatility, playing both second row and back row, may have counted against him as a question mark with Welsh coaches. Gloucester next face champions Northampton on Saturday.

lead.why: It is a new item about Wales's own squad selection, and the higher-scoring Adams and Basham items are club-side stories.

teams.heading: Contepomi's Pumas face Ireland, Italy and France in three November tests
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi's side opens its three-match European tour against Ireland in Dublin, then faces Italy in Genoa and France in Saint-Denis before the finals weekend in London. Argentina enter November fourth in the Southern Hemisphere standings with seven championship points, one behind third-placed Australia, and the coverage frames the tour as a chance to close that gap. Their July results were a win over Wales and defeats to Scotland and England.

lead.why: It is the only genuinely new item in the shortlist, and it sets out Argentina's full November Nations Championship tour.

teams.heading: Kurtley Beale recalled to Wallabies squad five years after last Test
teams.body: Kurtley Beale answered Les Kiss's SOS call to join the Wallabies' spring tour of the UK, replacing midfielder Hunter Paisami, who is unavailable for personal reasons. The 37-year-old has 95 Test caps and last played for Australia against Wales in Cardiff in 2021. The Guardian reports Kiss is seemingly considering backing a proven No 10 to end the revolving door at five-eighth, with James Ramm and Kalani Thomas also added to the touring group.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby publishes 2026 Nations Championship schedule, with Wales in Round 4
teams.body: Japan's 2026 Nations Championship schedule is out, and the next fixture on it is Wales in Round 4. Japan sit 10 of 12 on the log after three matches, with one win and two defeats, most recently a 28-34 loss to Fiji. Their 62 points scored and 88 conceded leave a points difference of -26. Next up is the trip to Wales.

lead.why: The only men's XV item in the pack; the other fresh items cover Wales women's WXV.

teams.heading: Richie Mo'unga ahead of schedule from calf injury, Tana Umaga says
teams.body: Richie Mo'unga is ahead of schedule from the calf injury that ruled him out of both Bledisloe Cup tests, Tana Umaga says. Rennie initially put recovery at six to eight weeks, with the worst case ruling the fly-half out of most of November's games, yet Mo'unga has been named in the 36-man squad. Umaga said: "He's being managed through and he's well ahead of where we thought he would be at." Mo'unga has been pushing to be back before the England match.

lead.why: A new, concrete fitness update on a key fly-half that gives fans a clear return timeline for the northern tour.

teams.heading: Nick Mallett rates uncapped Yaqeen Ahmed above Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu at fly-half
teams.body: Nick Mallett has put Yaqeen Ahmed ahead of Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu in the fly-half conversation, calling the Stormers rookie a 'no-frills fly-half' who 'doesn't make many mistakes'. Speaking on the Talking Boks podcast, the former Springboks coach praised Ahmed's hands and kicking game, though he said the 20-year-old still needs work on communication. With Handré Pollard out injured this window, Ahmed and Luan Giliomee will compete with Feinberg-Mngomezulu and Manie Libbok for the November matches against Italy, France and Ireland.

lead.why: A new, fan-friendly fly-half storyline, and Mallett's comparison goes straight to the Pollard-less November selection question.
